title: Iterators, generators, and decorators

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
Generators save memory by producing one item at a time from a large file or result stream; consume them deliberately.
CORE EXPLANATION
An iterator provides the next value through
next()

; a generator implements that protocol with yield and can process a large stream without loading it all into memory. A decorator wraps a function to add shared behavior such as timing, logging, or input checks. Use abstractions when they improve readability and testability.
EXAMPLE CODE
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.
EXPECTED RESULT

LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`def squares(limit):` — Creates reusable behavior; without the definition, callers cannot invoke or share this rule.
`for number in range(limit):` — Processes each iterable item; without the loop, remaining items are skipped.
`yield number * number` — This line continues the calculation or control flow; omitting it removes that step and may change later results.
`print(list(squares(4)))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

REMEMBER
yield produces the next item while preserving the generator's suspended state.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: A generator produces values on demand; create a new one if the stream must be traversed again.

spans.title: Important detail
spans.text: Generators can reduce peak memory use for files, paginated results, and transformation pipelines.

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: Mutating a collection while iterating can be surprising; build a new collection or iterate over a copy.
COMMON MISTAKES
Choose list, tuple, set, or dict based on ordering, uniqueness, and mutability needs.
